record.paper_title: Ten Open Problems in Connexive Logic
record.context_brief: Non-standard modalities on the Bochum plan
record.original_question: Determine whether FDE-based modal logics, including the connexive modal logic CK, admit interesting applications when one introduces non-standard modalities by keeping the familiar support of truth or falsity conditions for modal operators and modifying the opposite support conditions instead.

evidence.quote: Open problem 10 Are there interesting applications of systems of FDE-based modal logics (including the connexive modal logic CK in particular) with non-standard modalities obtained by keeping familiar support of truth (falsity) conditions of the modalities and tweaking their support of falsity (truth) conditions?
Based on these considerations, we leave the following problem, which may seem to be more like a research proposal.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. First-Degree Entailment (FDE) is a four-valued logic in which each formula is independently assigned a "support of truth" relation ⊨⁺ and a "support of falsity" relation ⊨⁻ at points of a model. An FDE-based modal logic extends FDE by unary modal operators (e.g. □, ◇) whose semantics is given by two clauses: a support-of-truth clause and a support-of-falsity clause, each typically quantifying over accessible worlds. In the standard "Bochum plan" approach to connexive modal logic, the connexive modal logic CK is obtained by retaining classical-style support-of-truth conditions for the modalities while modifying the support-of-falsity conditions so as to validate connexive principles (Aristotle's and Boethius' theses). One may, more generally, design "non-standard" modalities by fixing the familiar support-of-truth (resp. support-of-falsity) clauses for □ and ◇ and altering only the dual support-of-falsity (resp. support-of-truth) clauses.

Problem. Exhibit substantive applications — for instance to the analysis of natural-language modal discourse, to the formalization of normative, epistemic, deontic, or constructive reasoning, to information-based or paraconsistent reasoning, or to mathematically motivated semantic phenomena — of FDE-based modal logics, and in particular of the connexive modal logic CK, equipped with such non-standard modal operators obtained by keeping the familiar support-of-truth (falsity) clauses fixed and tweaking the support-of-falsity (truth) clauses. Either provide such applications together with a logical analysis demonstrating their interest, or argue that no such interesting applications exist.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as a research-proposal-style open problem about applications of FDE-based connexive modal logics with non-standard modalities. Recent works (e.g., Olkhovikov's 2025 paper on connexivity in modal and conditional contexts, and the Springer chapter "Another Generalization of Connexive Logic C") continue to study such systems, but no source identifies a definitive set of "interesting applications" that resolves the proposal. Status appears open.

status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work continuing investigation of connexive modal systems over FDE.
status_evidence.claim: Active subsequent research on connexive modal logics, but no resolution of the applications question is reported.

status_evidence.title: Connexive Variants of Modal Logics Over FDE
status_evidence.snippet: Studies FDE-based connexive modal systems via Bochum-plan tweaks.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the technical setting but does not settle the question of interesting applications.
